mainTopic: Honesty with non-Jews: robbery, lost items and business mistakes, דינא דמלכותא דינא and taxes, possibly stolen animals, and testifying for a גוי against a Jew.
overview: This amud deals with honest dealings with non-Jews. A ברייתא requires a fair reckoning with the non-Jewish owner of a Jewish slave. רב יוסף's attempt to limit this to a גר תושב is knocked down by אביי, so רבא splits the cases differently: actual גזל is forbidden, while letting a loan go unpaid is not. Next, רבי שמעון חסידא rules that robbing a גוי is forbidden but his lost item need not be returned, unless keeping it causes חילול השם. שמואל allows keeping a גוי's own business mistake, and stories about שמואל, רב כהנא, רבינא and רב אשי illustrate this. The גמרא then discusses שמואל's rule דינא דמלכותא דינא, proving it from the king's bridges and applying it to tax collection. רבא forbids buying animals from pen keepers near town, since they may be stolen. The amud ends with רבא's announcement that a Jew who volunteers testimony for a גוי against a fellow Jew in a gentile court is put in נידוי, and the reason continues on the next amud.

steps.title: You must deal honestly with the owner of a Jewish slave
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends by teaching that when a Jew sold to a non-Jew is redeemed, he may not be taken by force, and his owner may not be shortchanged. This is a challenge to the view that a גוי may be deceived.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא says you may not take the slave away by force so that he simply leaves. Someone might think you may shortchange the owner. So the פסוק says: "He shall reckon with his buyer." This teaches that you must be exact and fair with the buyer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting a ברייתא that forbids grabbing or cheating when you free a Jew from his non-Jewish owner. It uses this ברייתא to challenge the view, just before this section, that a גוי may be deceived.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק "וחשב עם קונהו" requires an exact, fair calculation with the buyer. If the Torah insists on honest dealing even here, where freeing a Jew is at stake, it seems that cheating a גוי is forbidden. That contradicts the earlier view that allowed it.

keyTerms.meaning: Pull him away (here, taking the slave by force)
He shall reckon with his buyer (ויקרא 25:50)

phrases.english: That one should not pull him out so that he leaves.
phrases.notes: He means: don't just grab the Jewish slave away from his non-Jewish owner by force.

phrases.english: One might think he may shortchange him?
So the verse says: "And he shall reckon with his buyer"
He must be exact with his buyer!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a ברייתא that began just before this section and is used as a challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view, quoted just before this section, that a גוי may be deceived.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The Torah demands an exact, fair reckoning with the non-Jewish buyer, so cheating a non-Jew must be forbidden.

steps.title: רב יוסף: a regular גוי versus a גר תושב
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף explains that deceiving is allowed with a regular גוי, while the ברייתא's demand for honesty is about a גר תושב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: This is not a difficulty. One ruling is about a regular גוי, and the other is about a גר תושב.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף resolves the contradiction by saying the two sources deal with two different kinds of non-Jews.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The view that allows deceiving speaks of an ordinary גוי. The ברייתא that demands an exact reckoning speaks of a גר תושב, a non-Jew who has accepted the seven Noahide מצוות. So the two sources do not clash.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-Jew living in ארץ ישראל who keeps the seven Noahide מצוות

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: It is not a difficulty;
this one is about a regular gentile,
that one is about a ger toshav.
phrases.notes: A non-Jew living in ארץ ישראל who accepted the seven Noahide מצוות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the ברייתא in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: each source deals with a different kind of non-Jew.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed both sources speak about the same kind of non-Jew, so they seemed to contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Deceiving is allowed with a regular גוי, while honest reckoning is required with a גר תושב.

steps.title: אביי: the פסוק mentions both side by side
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רב יוסף: the same פסוקים speak about both a גר תושב and a regular גוי, so how can the rule be split between them? He begins quoting a ברייתא to show this.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: But both of them are written right next to each other! The ברייתא teaches that the poor Jew sells himself not to you, but to a stranger, as it says "to a stranger." And not to a convert, but to a גר תושב, as it says "to a resident stranger."
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רב יוסף's answer and starts quoting a ברייתא on the פסוק of a Jew who sells himself as a slave. The ברייתא's first part shows that the פסוק speaks of a גר תושב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא reads ויקרא 25:47 word by word: "לגר" means a non-Jew rather than a fellow Jew, and "תושב" means a גר תושב rather than a גר צדק. אביי is setting up his point that the same section also includes a regular גוי.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him,
But both of them are written next to each other:
He sells himself not to you, but to a stranger –
phrases.notes: The ברייתא is about a poor Jew who sells himself as a slave (ויקרא 25:47).

phrases.english: as it says: "to a stranger."

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא לְגֵר צֶדֶק, אֶלָּא לְגֵר תּוֹשָׁב –
phrases.english: And not to a righteous convert, but to a ger toshav –
as it says: "to a resident stranger."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי, וְהָא תַּרְוַיְיהוּ גַּבֵּי הֲדָדֵי כְּתִיבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יוסף's split from step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's distinction between a regular גוי and a גר תושב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both kinds of non-Jew appear in the same section of פסוקים, so the honesty rule in that section should cover both.

steps.title: The same section includes a regular גוי
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: "the family of a stranger" means a regular גוי, and "the offshoot" means a Jew sold to serve עבודה זרה. So the honesty rule covers a regular גוי too, which contradicts רב יוסף.
steps.simpleTranslation: "The family of a stranger" means the גוי. When it says "or to the offshoot," that means one who is sold to serve עבודה זרה.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי finishes his proof: the very same פסוק also speaks of a regular גוי, so the command to reckon honestly with the buyer applies to him as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since "משפחת גר" refers to a regular גוי, and "וחשב עם קונהו" comes later in the same section, the honesty rule covers him too. That knocks out רב יוסף's claim that only a גר תושב must be dealt with honestly.

keyTerms.meaning: The family of a stranger (here, a regular גוי)

steps.whatToRemember: רב יוסף tried to limit the honesty rule to a גר תושב, but אביי shows that the same section of פסוקים includes a regular גוי, so "וחשב עם קונהו" seems to apply to him too.

phrases.english: "The family of a stranger" – this is the gentile;
when it says: "or to the offshoot" –
this is one who is sold to idol worship!
phrases.notes: Later in that same section the פסוק says "וחשב עם קונהו," so the honesty rule covers the plain גוי too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא that אביי began in step 3 and completes his challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's answer that only a גר תושב must be dealt with honestly.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The section that ends with "וחשב עם קונהו" explicitly includes a regular גוי, so you cannot say the honesty rule applies only to a גר תושב.

steps.title: רבא's new answer: robbery versus cancelling a loan
steps.stepSummary: רבא resolves the contradiction differently. The slave case involves actual robbery, while the other case only involves cancelling a debt.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: There is no contradiction. Here it is about robbing him, and there it is about cancelling his loan.
steps.whatsHappening: Since רב יוסף's split between a גר תושב and a regular גוי fell apart, רבא offers a completely new way to explain why the two sources disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא does not divide by type of non-Jew. He divides by type of action. Taking the slave away by trickery is real גזל, and that is forbidden even from a גוי. Misleading a גוי so that a debt goes unpaid is only הפקעת הלוואה, which does not take any actual money from him.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (we drop the earlier answer and try a new one)
It is not difficult; there is no contradiction
Robbing him (actually taking what is his)
Cancelling or escaping his loan, so a debt goes unpaid

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two cases. 'Here' (robbery) is the slave case, where honesty is required. 'There' (cancelling a loan) is the case where misleading a גוי is allowed.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said: It is not difficult;
here, it is about robbing him,
phrases.notes: 'Here' is the slave case, where the owner may not be shortchanged.

phrases.english: and there, it is about cancelling his loan.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב יוסף's answer, which אביי disproved in steps 3-4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases by type of action (robbery versus cancelling a loan)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two sources disagree about whether a גוי may be misled.
steps.terutzMaskana: Actual גזל of a גוי is forbidden. Cancelling a גוי's loan through misleading him is permitted.

steps.title: אביי objects: a Hebrew slave is just like a loan
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues that freeing a עבד עברי early is really only cancelling a debt, so it should fall under the permitted category.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: A Hebrew slave is a case of cancelling his loan!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רבא's answer. He claims the slave case is not robbery at all but just a debt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The master paid money for the slave, and the slave works it off over time, much like paying back a loan. If so, getting the slave out early by trickery would only be הפקעת הלוואה. Yet the ברייתא forbids it, which seems to break רבא's split.

keyTerms.meaning: A Jewish (Hebrew) slave, here one sold to a non-Jew

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
A Hebrew slave is a case of cancelling his loan!
phrases.notes: The idea is that the price the master paid works like a loan the slave pays back by working.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: עֶבֶד עִבְרִי הַפְקָעַת הַלְווֹאָתוֹ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's answer from step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that the slave case counts as robbery
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A עבד עברי's service only pays off money owed, so freeing him is just cancelling a loan. That is the permitted category, yet the ברייתא forbids it.

steps.title: רבא holds that a Hebrew slave's body is owned
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא defends רבא. In his view the master actually owns the slave's body, so taking him away is real robbery.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא follows his own reasoning, as רבא said: A Hebrew slave's body is owned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers אביי by pointing to another ruling of רבא, which shows the slave case really is robbery.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the slave were only a debt, אביי would be right. But רבא holds elsewhere that the master owns the עבד עברי's body itself. Taking him away by trickery therefore takes the master's actual property, which is גזל, and that stays forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Following his own reasoning (consistent with his view elsewhere)
His body is owned (the master has real ownership, not just a debt)

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's rule: actually taking a גוי's property (including a slave whose body is owned) is forbidden, while misleading him so a loan goes unpaid is permitted.

phrases.english: Rava follows his own reasoning,
as Rava said:
A Hebrew slave's body is owned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge from step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Pointing to the speaker's consistent view elsewhere (לטעמיה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A עבד עברי is only a debt, so freeing him is cancelling a loan.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבא the slave's body is owned, so taking him is real robbery and is forbidden.

steps.title: Robbing a non-Jew is forbidden, but his lost item may be kept
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון חסידא rules that גזל from a גוי is forbidden, but one does not have to return a גוי's אבידה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ביבי בר גידל said that רבי שמעון חסידא said: Robbing a non-Jew is forbidden, and keeping his lost item is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new, related teaching about money matters with a גוי. It gives two short rules that the next steps will each back up with a source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two different actions get two different rulings. Actively taking a גוי's property is forbidden. Simply not returning something he lost is allowed.

phrases.english: Rav Beivai bar Giddel said
that Rabbi Shimon Chasida said:
Robbing a non-Jew is forbidden,
his lost item is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב בִּיבִי בַּר גִּידֵּל אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן חֲסִידָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new, related teaching about money dealings with a גוי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: גזל from a גוי is forbidden, while a גוי's אבידה does not need to be returned.

steps.title: The source that robbing a non-Jew is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא learns from a פסוק that a גוי's property may be taken only in war, when the nations are handed over to you, and not otherwise.
steps.simpleTranslation: Robbing him is forbidden, as רב הונא said: From where do we know that robbing a non-Jew is forbidden? As it says, "And you shall consume all the peoples that ה׳ your God gives to you." That means when they are handed over into your hand, and not when they are not handed over into your hand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the first half of רבי שמעון חסידא's teaching by bringing רב הונא's source from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק permits 'consuming' the nations only when ה׳ 'gives' them to you, which means a time of war. From the condition we learn the reverse: when they are not handed over to you, their property is off-limits.

keyTerms.meaning: Handed over into your hand (under your control, as in war)

phrases.english: Robbing him is forbidden —
as Rav Huna said:
From where do we know that robbing a non-Jew is forbidden?
As it is stated: "And you shall consume all the peoples
that ה׳ your God gives to you" —
at a time when they are handed over into your hand,
and not at a time when they are not handed over into your hand.

steps.triggerLanguage: גְּזֵילוֹ אָסוּר דְּאָמַר רַב הוּנָא: מִנַּיִן לְגֶזֶל הַגּוֹי שֶׁהוּא אָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the first ruling in step 8.
steps.raayaObject: That גזל from a גוי is forbidden
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברים 7:16, read as permitting the nations' property only when they are handed over to you

steps.title: The source that a non-Jew's lost item need not be returned
steps.stepSummary: רב, quoted by רב חמא בר גוריא, learns from the words 'your brother' that the מצוה of returning lost items applies to a fellow Jew and not to a גוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: His lost item is permitted, as רב חמא בר גוריא said in the name of רב: From where do we know that a non-Jew's lost item is permitted? As it says, "With every lost thing of your brother." To your brother you return it, and you do not return it to a non-Jew.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the second half of רבי שמעון חסידא's teaching by bringing a source from the פסוק about returning lost items.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מצוה of השבת אבידה is said about 'your brother.' That word limits the obligation to a fellow Jew, so there is no duty to return a גוי's lost item. This is different from robbery, because here you are only failing to give something back, not taking it.
steps.whatToRemember: Two separate rules: גזל from a גוי is forbidden (learned from דברים 7:16), while returning a גוי's אבידה is not required (learned from 'your brother' in דברים 22:3).

phrases.english: His lost item is permitted —

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב חָמָא בַּר גּוּרְיָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: as Rav Chama bar Gurya said that Rav said:
From where do we know that a non-Jew's lost item is permitted?
As it is stated: "With every lost thing of your brother" —
to your brother you return it,
and you do not return it to a non-Jew.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבֵידָתוֹ מוּתֶּרֶת דְּאָמַר רַב חָמָא בַּר גּוּרְיָא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the second ruling in step 8, matching step 9.
steps.raayaObject: That a גוי's אבידה need not be returned
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברים 22:3, where 'your brother' limits the מצוה to a fellow Jew

steps.title: Maybe the exemption only covers an item not yet picked up
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב's derivation. Maybe 'your brother' only frees you from searching for a גוי's lost item. Once it is in your hand, perhaps you must return it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say this applies only where the item has not come into his hand, so he does not have to go after it. But where it has come into his hand, say he should return it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions how far רב's lesson from 'your brother' goes. It suggests the exemption might only mean you don't have to go looking for a גוי's lost item.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two stages to returning an אבידה: taking care to pick it up, and giving it back once you have it. The challenge says the פסוק might only cancel the first stage for a גוי. Once the item is actually in your hands, you might still have to return it.

keyTerms.meaning: But say (introduces a different possible reading)
This applies (only in a certain case)

phrases.english: But say that this applies
where the item has not come into his hand,
that he is not obligated to go looking for it;
but where it has come into his hand,
say that he should return it!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵימָא הָנֵי מִילֵּי הֵיכָא דְּלָא אֲתַי לִידֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the scope of רב's derivation from 'your brother' in Step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's derivation that a גוי's אבידה need not be returned
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק could be read narrowly, as freeing you only from searching. It may not free you from returning an item you already hold.

steps.title: The word 'and you found it' covers an item already in hand
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers that the פסוק says 'וּמְצָאתָהּ'. That word describes an item that has already reached your hand, so the exemption covers that case too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: The פסוק says 'and you have found it,' which means the item has already come into his hand.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers the challenge by pointing to a word in the same פסוק. 'And you have found it' is talking about an item you are already holding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מצוה of returning, with its limit to 'your brother', is stated about an item that was already found. So the limit applies to an item in your hand as well. A גוי's אבידה does not have to be returned even after you pick it up.

phrases.english: Ravina said:
"and you have found it"
implies that it has come into his hand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual proof from a word in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The exemption might only cover searching for an item not yet found.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק speaks of an item already found, so even an item in hand need not be returned to a גוי.

steps.title: Where there is חילול השם, even a lost item must be returned
steps.stepSummary: רבי פנחס בן יאיר teaches in a ברייתא that keeping even a גוי's lost item is forbidden where it would cause חילול השם.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי פנחס בן יאיר says: In a place where there is חילול השם, even keeping his lost item is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא adds an important exception to the rule just set out. If keeping a גוי's lost item would cause חילול השם, you may not keep it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The basic rule is still that there is no מצוה to return a גוי's אבידה. But a separate concern can override it: if keeping the item would make people think badly of the Torah and the Jewish people, it is forbidden. The word 'אפילו' (even) ties back to Step 8, where גזל from a גוי was already forbidden.
steps.whyThisMatters: This exception limits the permission to keep a גוי's lost item in practice, so the rule is never applied in a way that disgraces ה׳'s name.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי פִּנְחָס בֶּן יָאִיר אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair says:
In a place where there is desecration of ה׳'s name,
even his lost item is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי פִּנְחָס בֶּן יָאִיר אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds an exception to the rule that a גוי's אבידה need not be returned.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Where keeping a גוי's lost item would cause חילול השם, it is forbidden to keep it.
steps.whatToRemember: A גוי's אבידה does not have to be returned, even after you pick it up. But where keeping it would cause חילול השם, it must be returned.

steps.title: שמואל: a גוי's business mistake may be kept
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that you may benefit from a גוי's own mistake in a deal, without correcting it.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: His mistake is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a related topic. שמואל rules that if a גוי makes a mistake in a business deal, you do not have to fix it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This parallels the rule about a lost item. A mistake the גוי made himself is treated like money he lost, not like money taken from him. So it is not considered גזל, which Step 8 already ruled is forbidden.
steps.confusionAlert: שמואל only allows keeping a mistake the גוי made on his own. Actively stealing from or tricking a גוי is still forbidden as גזל (Step 8).

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
His mistake is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the topic from a גוי's lost item to a גוי's business mistake.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Profit from a גוי's own business mistake does not have to be returned.

steps.title: שמואל buys a gold bowl at the price of iron
steps.stepSummary: שמואל himself bought a golden bowl that the גוי thought was iron, paying the iron price of four זוז.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like that incident where שמואל bought from a גוי a golden bowl as if it were iron, for four זוז, and he worked one זוז into the payment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up שמואל's ruling with a story of what he himself did. The גוי thought his bowl was iron, and שמואל bought it at the iron price.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גוי made the mistake himself by thinking his gold bowl was iron. שמואל did not correct him, which matches his ruling that a גוי's mistake may be kept. The story shows the ruling was actually followed in practice.

keyTerms.meaning: In exchange for / as if it were iron

phrases.english: Like that incident of Shmuel,
who bought from a gentile a golden bowl
at the price of iron, for four zuz,
and he worked one zuz into the payment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates שמואל's ruling in Step 14 with his own action.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's ruling that a גוי's mistake is permitted
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל's own purchase of a golden bowl at the price of iron

steps.title: רב כהנא buys 120 barrels for the price of 100
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא bought 120 barrels for the price of 100. He told the גוי that he was relying on him, so the counting was the גוי's job.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא bought from a גוי 120 barrels for the price of 100, and worked one זוז into the payment. He said to him: See, I am relying on you.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second story of benefiting from a גוי's mistake. The גוי miscounted and sold 120 barrels as if they were 100.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Again the mistake was the גוי's own. רב כהנא said 'I am relying on you,' which put the job of checking on the גוי. He did not make any false statement himself.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana bought from a gentile
one hundred and twenty barrels for the price of one hundred,
and he worked one zuz into the payment;
he said to him: See,
that I am relying on you.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב כָּהֲנָא זְבַן מִגּוֹי מְאָה וְעֶשְׂרִין חָבְיָתָא בִּמְאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second story supporting שמואל's ruling.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's ruling that a גוי's mistake is permitted
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב כהנא's purchase of 120 barrels for the price of 100

steps.title: רבינא takes the thicker logs from the trunk
steps.stepSummary: רבינא and a גוי bought a palm tree together to chop up. רבינא told his attendant to take his share from the thick trunk, since the גוי only counts the number of logs.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא and a גוי bought a palm tree to chop up. He said to his attendant: Hurry and bring my share from the trunk, because the גוי only knows the number.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third story. רבינא split a palm tree with a גוי, and the גוי was only counting logs, not checking their size.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גוי's mistake was thinking that only the number of pieces mattered. רבינא took advantage of that by taking the thicker pieces from the trunk. This fits the same rule: you may benefit from a גוי's own mistake.

phrases.english: Ravina bought a palm tree,
he and a gentile together, to chop it up;
he said to his attendant:
Hurry and bring my share from the trunk,
for the gentile knows only the number.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבִינָא זְבַן דִּיקְלָא הוּא וְגוֹי לְצַלָּחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third story supporting שמואל's ruling.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's ruling that a גוי's mistake is permitted
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבינא's division of a palm tree with a גוי

steps.title: רב אשי asks for grapes only if they belong to a גוי
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי saw grapes in an orchard. He told his attendant to bring some only if the vine belonged to a גוי, not if it belonged to a Jew.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי was walking on the road and saw a grapevine branch in an orchard with clusters of grapes hanging on it. He said to his attendant: Go see. If they belong to a גוי, bring some. If they belong to a Jew, don't bring me any.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a final story. רב אשי makes a distinction between a גוי's grapes and a Jew's grapes, and this sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At first glance it looks as if רב אשי permits taking a גוי's property. That would contradict Step 8, which ruled that גזל from a גוי is forbidden. The next step raises exactly this problem.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi was walking on the road;
he saw a branch of a grapevine in an orchard,
and clusters of grapes were hanging on it.
He said to his attendant: Go see;
if they belong to a gentile, bring some.

phrases.aramaic: אִי דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל נִינְהוּ – לָא אַיְיתִי לִי.
phrases.english: If they belong to a Jew, do not bring me any.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new story, which sets up a question about whether taking from a גוי is allowed.
steps.raayaObject: How to deal properly with a גוי's property
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב אשי's instruction about the grapes

steps.title: The גוי asks: is a גוי's property permitted?
steps.stepSummary: A גוי sitting in the orchard overheard and asked רב אשי whether a גוי's property is permitted to take.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain גוי who was sitting in the orchard heard this. He said to him: Is a גוי's property permitted?!
steps.whatsHappening: A גוי who was sitting in the orchard overheard and challenged רב אשי. He asks whether it is allowed to take a גוי's grapes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge sounds like it is aimed at רב אשי's words. But really it raises the question in הלכה of whether he was permitting גזל from a גוי. That would go against Step 8, which forbids it.

phrases.english: A certain gentile heard,
who was sitting in the orchard;
he said to him: Is a gentile's property permitted?!

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמַע הָהוּא גּוֹי דַּהֲוָה יָתֵיב בְּפַרְדֵּיסָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב אשי's instruction from Step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's distinction between a גוי's grapes and a Jew's grapes
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רב אשי allows taking a גוי's grapes, he seems to permit גזל from a גוי.

steps.title: רב אשי: a גוי accepts payment, a Jew does not
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that he meant to pay. A גוי accepts money for his grapes, but a Jewish owner would not accept payment.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: A גוי takes money for them. A Jew does not take money for them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers that he never planned to take anything for free. He intended to pay, and only a גוי would let him pay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His distinction was about paying, not about stealing. A גוי would accept the price, so buying from him is fine. A Jewish owner would refuse the money, so רב אשי would end up taking the grapes for nothing. This confirms that taking a גוי's property without paying is forbidden.
steps.whatToRemember: There is no מצוה to return a גוי's אבידה, and a גוי's own business mistake may be kept. But גזל from a גוי is forbidden, and so is anything that causes חילול השם. רב אשי only meant to take the grapes by paying for them.

phrases.english: He said to him:
A gentile accepts money,
a Jew does not accept money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the גוי's challenge in Step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the case (it was buying, not taking)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב אשי seemed to permit taking a גוי's grapes for free.
steps.terutzMaskana: He meant to pay. Only a גוי would accept payment, while a Jew would refuse it.

steps.title: שמואל's rule: the law of the kingdom is the law
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to שמואל's rule, דינא דמלכותא דינא: the laws of the government are binding.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now back to the rule itself. שמואל says: The law of the kingdom is the law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a rule of שמואל that was quoted earlier and is now going to discuss it directly. This step sets up the proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, שמואל's rule was mentioned in passing. Now the גמרא puts it in the center. The rule says that a Jew must treat the government's laws as real, binding law.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter itself. Used to go back and look closely at a statement quoted earlier.
The law of the kingdom is the law: government laws are binding.

steps.whyThisMatters: This is one of the most important rules in practical הלכה. It is the basis for treating taxes and government property laws as binding.

phrases.english: The matter itself: Shmuel says:
The law of the kingdom is the law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the stories of רב כהנא, רבינא and רב אשי about dealing with a גוי, and returns to שמואל's rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The government's law is binding הלכה.

steps.title: רבא's proof from the king's bridges
steps.stepSummary: רבא proves שמואל's rule. The government cuts down people's palm trees to build bridges, and we still cross those bridges.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: You can see this is true. The government cuts down palm trees and builds bridges from them, and we walk over those bridges.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a proof from everyday life that the king's law really counts as law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The trees were taken from their owners without permission. If that counted as stealing, using the bridges would mean using stolen property. Since everyone crosses them, the king's taking must be legal.

keyTerms.meaning: Know that this is so. Introduces a proof.

phrases.english: Rava said: Know that this is so,
for they cut down palm trees
phrases.notes: "They" are the king's officials, and they take the trees without asking the owners.

phrases.english: and build bridges,
and we cross over them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports שמואל's rule with a real-life practice.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The accepted practice of crossing bridges built from trees the government took.

steps.title: אביי: maybe the owners simply gave up hope
steps.stepSummary: אביי pushes back on the proof. Perhaps the bridges are allowed only because the owners gave up hope of getting their trees back (יאוש).
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: But maybe it is because the owners gave up hope of getting them back!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי offers a different reason why we may cross the bridges, which would weaken רבא's proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the owners' יאוש is the real reason, the bridges tell us nothing about the king's law. Then רבא's case does not prove שמואל's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: They gave up hope, from the word יאוש.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
But perhaps it is because they gave up hope
of them, meaning their owners did!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's proof by offering another reason for the practice.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof is rejected, not שמואל's rule itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The practice could be explained by the owners' יאוש instead of the king's law.

steps.title: רבא: giving up hope only works because the king's law is valid
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that without דינא דמלכותא דינא, the owners' יאוש would not make the wood permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: If the law of the kingdom were not the law, how would the owners' giving up hope help?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends his proof by showing that אביי's reason depends on שמואל's rule anyway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Giving up hope alone does not move ownership. The wood would still belong to the owners. It is only because the king's taking is legal that the wood really leaves the owners, so the proof stands.

keyTerms.meaning: If not, meaning if it were not so.

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not denying that the owners gave up hope. He is saying their יאוש is not enough by itself. It only works together with the king's legal right.

phrases.english: He said to him:
If the law of the kingdom were not the law,
how would their giving up hope help?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִי לָא דִּינָא דְמַלְכוּתָא דִּינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's pushback.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the other explanation itself depends on the rule being proven.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The owners' יאוש alone explains why the bridges are permitted.
steps.terutzMaskana: יאוש only works because the king's taking is legal, so the proof for שמואל stands.

steps.title: But the officials don't follow the king's orders
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the officials disobey the king. He told them to cut a little from every valley, but they cut everything from one valley.
steps.simpleTranslation: But they are not doing what the king said! The king said: Go and cut from all the valleys. They went and cut it all from one valley.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא's proof. The officials are not acting according to the king's law, so the king's law cannot explain the practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דינא דמלכותא covers what the king actually commands. When officials break his order and load the whole loss onto one valley, that looks like plain robbery, not the king's law.

phrases.english: But they do not act
as the king said:
The king said:
Go and cut from all the valleys,
and they go and cut
from one valley!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא לָא קָא עָבְדִי כִּדְאָמַר מַלְכָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof survives אביי, a new attack comes on the facts of the case.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The officials act against the king's order, so their taking is not covered by דינא דמלכותא.

steps.title: The king's agent is like the king, and the owners can collect from others
steps.stepSummary: The king's agent has the king's authority and does not have to go to the trouble of cutting from every valley. The owners who lost trees should collect payment from the people of all the valleys.
steps.simpleTranslation: The king's agent is like the king, and he does not have to bother. The owners caused their own loss, because they should have collected from all the valleys and taken money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Cutting from one valley is still within the king's authority, so רבא's proof stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The agent stands in the king's place and may take the easy route of one valley. Fairness is kept another way: the owners who lost trees may collect payment from everyone else. If they don't, the loss is their own fault.

keyTerms.meaning: The king's agent is like the king.
They caused a loss to themselves.

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל: דינא דמלכותא דינא. רבא proves it from the king's bridges. Neither יאוש nor the agents cutting from one valley weakens the proof, because the agent acts with the king's authority and the owners can collect from everyone else.

phrases.english: The king's agent is like the king,
and he does not go to the trouble;
and they caused a loss to themselves,
phrases.notes: "They" are the owners whose trees were cut.

phrases.english: for they should have collected
phrases.notes: Some versions say the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording. Both mean "to collect."

phrases.english: from all the valleys,
and taken money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge about the officials breaking the king's order.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case: the agent's action counts as the king's, and the fairness problem is solved by the owners collecting from others.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Cutting from one valley is outside the king's order, so it counts as robbery.
steps.terutzMaskana: The agent has the king's authority to take from one place. The owners can collect payment from all the valleys, so the taking is legal and the bridges may be used.

steps.title: Whoever is at the threshing floor pays the king's share
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that the king's collector may take the king's share of grain from whichever owner he finds at the threshing floor.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Whoever is found at the threshing floor pays the king's share.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new tax ruling. The king's collector does not have to search for every owner; he may take the whole king's share from whoever is there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fits the idea from step 26: the king's agent does not have to go to extra trouble. Collecting the whole amount from the person present is legal under דינא דמלכותא דינא, so it is not stealing.

keyTerms.meaning: The threshing floor, where the grain is gathered
The king's share of the crop (a tax)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא: מַאן דְּמִשְׁתְּכַח בְּבֵי דָרֵי,
phrases.english: Rava said: Whoever is found at the threshing floor,
pays the king's share.
phrases.notes: He pays the share for everyone who owns the field, not just his own part.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: מַאן דְּמִשְׁתְּכַח בְּבֵי דָרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ruling built on the same idea as step 26: the king's agent may collect in the easiest way.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The king's collector may take the whole king's share from whichever owner is found at the threshing floor.

steps.title: This applies to a partner, not a sharecropper
steps.stepSummary: The ruling only applies to a partner who owns part of the field. An אריס only takes his pay from the crop, so the tax may not be taken from him.
steps.simpleTranslation: This applies only to a partner. But a sharecropper is only taking out his sharecropping portion.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא limits רבא's ruling. Only a partner can be made to pay for everyone, not an אריס who works the field for a share of the crop.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A partner owns the land, so he is part of the group that owes the tax. An אריס does not own the land; his grain is just his wages, so taking the tax from it would be taking from someone who does not owe it.

keyTerms.meaning: A partner who owns part of the field
A sharecropper who works the field for part of the crop
And this rule applies only to...

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the אריס is free because he is poor. The reason is that he is not an owner, so the tax was never his to pay.

phrases.english: And this applies only to a partner,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אֲרִיסָא – אֲרִיסוּתֵיהּ הוּא דְּקָא מַפֵּיק.
phrases.english: but a sharecropper is only taking out his sharecropping portion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits step 27 to partners and leaves out sharecroppers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only a partner who owns part of the land may be made to pay the king's share for all the owners; a sharecropper may not.

steps.title: One townsman can be made to give security for another's tax
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that the tax collector may take one townsman's property as security for the tax another townsman owes.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: A townsman may be taken as security for another townsman.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a second tax ruling. People of the same town are responsible together, so the collector may take property from one of them for another's tax.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The town as a whole owes the king. So the collector may take a pledge from any resident, and that resident can later settle with the one who really owed.

keyTerms.meaning: Is taken as security (a pledge is taken from him)

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רָבָא: בַּר מָתָא אַבַּר מָתָא מִיעֲבָט.
phrases.english: And Rava said: A townsman may be made to give security for another townsman.
phrases.notes: The collector may take something of his as a pledge for the other person's unpaid tax.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָבָא: בַּר מָתָא אַבַּר מָתָא מִיעֲבָט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second tax ruling of רבא, following the same idea of shared responsibility to the king.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Property of one townsman may be taken as security for the tax of another townsman.

steps.title: Only for this year's taxes
steps.stepSummary: The security rule applies only to this year's land tax and head tax. For last year's tax it no longer applies, because the king has already been paid.
steps.simpleTranslation: This applies only to the land tax and head tax of this year. But for a year that has passed, since the king has already been satisfied, the right has passed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא limits רבא's second ruling to this year's taxes. Once the year is over and the king has his money, the collector may not take from one person for another's old debt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The special power exists to make sure the king gets paid. After the king is satisfied, whatever the collector is still owed is his own private debt, so he must collect it only from the person who owes it.

keyTerms.meaning: Head tax, paid by each person
The king has been satisfied (already paid)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the limit of דינא דמלכותא דינא: the king's agent gets special power only as far as the king's own need goes.

phrases.english: And this applies only to the land tax
and the head tax of this year,
but for a year that has passed,
since the king has already been satisfied, the right has passed.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָנֵי מִילֵּי דְּבֹרָלָא אַרְעָא וּכְרָגָא דְּהַאי שַׁתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits step 29 to the current year's taxes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A townsman's property may be taken for another's tax only for this year's taxes, not for past years once the king is paid.
steps.whatToRemember: The king's agent may collect the easy way (from whoever is present, or from any townsman), but not from an אריס, and not for old taxes after the king is paid.

steps.title: Do not buy from those who keep pens inside the town limits
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that it is forbidden to buy animals from people who keep animal pens inside the תחום of a town.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: Those who set up pens inside the town limits, it is forbidden to buy from them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא starts a new topic: buying animals that might be stolen. He forbids buying from people who keep pens near the town.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These people keep their herds close to the town's animals. The reason for the ban comes in the next two steps.

keyTerms.meaning: The limits of the town, the area around it

steps.confusionAlert: Here דָּרֵי means animal pens, not the threshing floor (בֵּי דָרֵי) from step 27. Same-looking word, different meaning.

phrases.english: And Rava said: Those who set up pens
phrases.notes: These are non-Jews who keep animals in pens on the town's fields.

phrases.english: inside the town limits, it is forbidden to buy from them.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָבָא: הָנֵי דְּדָיְירִי דָּרֵי בְּתוֹךְ הַתְּחוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ruling of רבא on a new topic: animals that might be stolen.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: It is forbidden to buy animals from those who keep pens inside the town limits.

steps.title: Why is it forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רבא's ban.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why buying from them is forbidden. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling in step 31 gave no reason. The question asks what makes these animals suspect.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind step 31.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why it is forbidden to buy animals from those who keep pens inside the town limits.

steps.title: The town's animals get mixed in with theirs
steps.stepSummary: The reason is that the town's animals mix in with their herds, so the animal you buy might belong to someone from the town.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the town's animals get mixed in with theirs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The animal being sold might really be someone else's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the pens are close to town, local animals can wander into the herd. Buying from them risks buying a stolen or lost animal that belongs to a townsperson.

phrases.english: Because the town's animals get mixed in with theirs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 32.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The town's animals get mixed into their herds, so what they sell may belong to a townsperson.

steps.title: Outside the town limits it is allowed
steps.stepSummary: If the pens are outside the תחום, buying from them is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Outside the town limits, it is allowed to buy from them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא's ruling continues with the other side. Far from town, buying is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason for the ban was mixing with the town's animals. Outside the תחום, that is unlikely, so the worry falls away.

phrases.english: Outside the town limits, it is allowed to buy from them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The other half of רבא's ruling, built on the reason given in step 33.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Buying animals from those whose pens are outside the town limits is allowed.

steps.title: If the owners chased their animals, it is forbidden even outside
steps.stepSummary: רבינא adds that if owners were seen chasing after animals, buying is forbidden even when the pens are outside the תחום.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: If owners were chasing after them, even outside the town limits it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא adds a limit to the permission of step 34. When there is a clear sign that animals went missing, buying is forbidden even far from town.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Outside the תחום was allowed only because mixing was unlikely. If owners are seen running after the herd, that shows their animals really did get in, so the worry comes back.
steps.whatToRemember: Buying from those with pens is forbidden inside the תחום and allowed outside it, unless owners were seen chasing their animals; then it is forbidden everywhere.

phrases.english: Ravina said: If owners were

phrases.aramaic: מְרַדְּפִים אַחֲרֵיהֶם, אֲפִילּוּ חוּץ לַתְּחוּם אָסוּר.
phrases.english: chasing after them, even outside the town limits it is forbidden.

steps.title: רבא's public ruling: excommunicate a Jew who testifies for a gentile against a fellow Jew
steps.stepSummary: רבא (or רב הונא) announced that a Jew who knows testimony helpful to a גוי, and goes on his own to testify for him in a gentile court against a fellow Jew, is put in נידוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא announced, and some say it was רב הונא: everyone, both those who go up to ארץ ישראל and those who go down to בבל, should know this. A Jew who knows testimony that helps a גוי, and goes and testifies for him in a gentile court against his fellow Jew, we put him in נידוי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic with a public announcement by רבא: a Jew who testifies for a גוי against a fellow Jew in a gentile court gets put in נידוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a fresh ruling, not connected to the animal-pen cases before it, except that both deal with Jews and non-Jews. The phrase about 'going up and going down' shows the ruling was meant for everyone, everywhere. The punishment is serious: נידוי, a formal ban.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who go up and those who go down, meaning everyone traveling between ארץ ישראל and בבל
We put him in נידוי (a formal ban)

steps.confusionAlert: The problem is not testifying in general. It is a Jew going on his own to a gentile court to help a גוי take money from a fellow Jew.

phrases.english: Rava announced,
and some say it was Rav Huna:
Those who go up,
phrases.notes: Going up means to ארץ ישראל and going down means to בבל, so this is addressed to everyone.

phrases.english: and those who go down —
this Jew
who knows testimony for a gentile
(and the gentile did not ask him for it),
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets, and some have them.

phrases.english: and goes and testifies for him
in a gentile court
against his fellow Jew —
we put him in a ban.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new ruling about Jews and non-Jews, following the earlier discussion of buying from herders.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A Jew who goes and testifies for a גוי in a gentile court against a fellow Jew is put in נידוי.

steps.title: Why is he excommunicated?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind this harsh punishment.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why such a Jew deserves נידוי. This sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Telling the truth is normally a good thing, so the punishment needs an explanation. The גמרא wants to know what exactly is wrong with this testimony.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind רבא's ruling in step 36.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a Jew who testifies for a גוי against a fellow Jew is put in נידוי.

steps.title: Because gentile courts take away money
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins its answer: gentile courts take money away from people, which the next lines will finish explaining.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because they, the gentile courts, take away money...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to give the reason: gentile courts take money from the Jew. The sentence is not finished here and continues in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is that his testimony causes a fellow Jew to lose money in a gentile court. The rest of the sentence will explain why this court's ruling is unfair by Torah standards.

phrases.english: because they take away money

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of step 37.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Gentile courts take money away from the Jew (explanation continues in the next lines).
